title: OpenAI Sponsored Agents: The Ad Is Now a Conversation You Cannot See
desc: OpenAI is testing Sponsored Agents in ChatGPT. The ad adapts to the conversation, the agent it hands you to does not, and Angi is already in the pilot.
keywords: openai sponsored agents, chatgpt sponsored agents, chatgpt ads conversation, ai search advertising, chatgpt ads for local business, sponsored agent pilot, ai advertising 2026
cta: Want a qualifying conversation that works on any surface?
body:
September 18, 2026. Angi, the home services marketplace, is now running an ad that never sends the homeowner to a website. On 16 September OpenAI began testing Sponsored Agents, an ad unit in ChatGPT that a person can click and then keep talking to, inside the chat, without ever landing on anybody's site. If you sell plumbing, HVAC, roofing or any other local service, the aggregator that already outranks you on Google has just bought a seat inside the conversation where your customer is describing the job.

The interesting part is not that ChatGPT has ads. It has had them for months. The interesting part is a pair of sentences in OpenAI's own announcement that point in opposite directions, and almost nobody has read them together.

What OpenAI actually shipped

OpenAI published Reimagining advertising with AI on 16 September 2026. Five things landed at once.

  1. Sponsored Agents. After seeing a relevant ad, a user "can choose to start a clearly labeled conversation with a business-sponsored agent in ChatGPT", ask follow up questions, and "follow a link to the business's website when they're ready to take the next step". Testing is limited to "select advertisers in the United States", so most businesses cannot buy one yet.
  2. Prompt to campaign. Advertisers can now use plain language prompts to create, update and analyse campaigns inside ChatGPT through the Ads Manager plugin, turning "a website or brief into a campaign".
  3. Generated creative. Ads Manager suggests copy and imagery drawn from your landing page and your campaign objective. OpenAI is explicit that you review and edit before anything goes live.
  4. Opt in text customisation. If you enable it, the system "adapts an advertiser's existing headlines and descriptions to better fit the context of a conversation" and automatically translates ad copy into the user's preferred language.
  5. CRM and commerce hooks. HubSpot is named as the first CRM partner and Shopify as the first ecommerce partner. The Shopify app becomes available internationally, in markets where ChatGPT Ads already run, on 23 September.

The context gap nobody is pricing

Put two sentences from that one announcement side by side.

On text customisation, OpenAI says the system "adapts an advertiser's existing headlines and descriptions to better fit the context of a conversation".

On Sponsored Agents, it says: "The conversation with a Sponsored Agent is distinct from ChatGPT's independent answers and separate from the original conversation that the user started in ChatGPT."

So the ad is tuned by the context. The agent the ad hands the person to is not. Your headline can be rewritten on the fly because ChatGPT knows the homeowner just said the dishwasher is leaking under a fitted counter. The agent you are paying to hold the next conversation opens on a blank page and has to ask again.

That is a defensible privacy boundary, and OpenAI states it openly rather than burying it. But it changes what you have to build. A Sponsored Agent is not a landing page with a chat widget bolted on. It is a first conversation with somebody who has already explained themselves once and will be annoyed to do it twice. The whole job is re-qualifying fast, in two or three questions, without sounding like a form.

Agencies that have built voice and chat intake already know this shape. It is the same problem as an after hours phone agent that cannot see the caller's history: the opening has to do the work. Businesses running AI call answering for home services have spent two years learning which three questions actually qualify a job, and that script is the transferable asset here, not the ad copy.

Angi got there first, and that is the tell

Angi confirmed on the same day that it is in the pilot. In its own words, an Angi branded sponsored agent "may appear in relevant ChatGPT conversations regarding home services", homeowners can "continue the conversation with the Angi agent to share more information about their project", and when the job needs a professional they "enter Angi's service request flow to connect with skilled local pros".

Read that as a contractor rather than as a marketer. The marketplace is not buying a click to its website. It is buying the qualification step, the part where the homeowner describes the job in their own words, and it is running that step inside the surface where the homeowner is already thinking out loud. The contractor still gets the work. The contractor gets it afterwards, as a purchased lead, at the marketplace's price.

That is the same trade contractors made when directories took the top of the search results, except the directory now sits one layer earlier, before a search result page is ever rendered. Nobody in the pilot list is a single location service business, because the pilot is closed. The question worth asking is what you do in the twelve to eighteen months before it opens.

Where the conversion event moved

Ads in ChatGPT are not new, and the buying model changed to CPC bidding earlier this month. What is new is that the click stops being the moment of intent.

In a normal paid channel, the click is the first thing the advertiser can see and roughly the point where persuasion ends. With a Sponsored Agent, OpenAI describes the link to your website as something the user follows "when they're ready to take the next step". The click now sits at the end of a conversation, not at the start of one. Everything that decided whether the person clicks happened inside OpenAI: which questions they asked, what worried them, what your agent said back.

Three practical consequences follow.

  1. Click through rate changes meaning. A lower CTR with a longer conversation in front of it is not automatically worse, and the number is no longer comparable to your Google Ads CTR.
  2. Your analytics see a warm visitor with no story attached. The qualification transcript is the most valuable thing produced by the ad, and it is produced on somebody else's infrastructure.
  3. Cost per lead becomes cost per conversation plus a conversion rate you did not previously have to model. If you quote clients on cost per click, that model breaks quietly rather than loudly.

What it means for operators

The honest summary is that this is a pilot, in one country, with a short list of advertisers, and anybody selling you a Sponsored Agents service today is selling you something they cannot buy. That does not make it ignorable, for three reasons.

First, the qualifying script is the durable asset and you can write it now. If you can already state the three questions that separate a real job from a tyre kicker, you have most of a Sponsored Agent. If you cannot, no ad platform will fix that.

Second, the CRM side is already live. HubSpot customers can create and measure ChatGPT ad campaigns without leaving HubSpot, which is the measurable half of this and the half you can test this quarter. We covered that integration when it launched, and the lesson then was that attribution is what makes a new channel defensible internally.

Third, aggregators move first in every channel, and the counter has never been to outbid them. It is to be the specific answer rather than the general one. That is ordinary AI automation and lead generation work: own the narrow query, answer it better than a marketplace can, and make sure the first conversation a customer has with you is competent whether it happens on your site, on your phone line, or inside somebody else's chat window.

What to do in the next two weeks

  1. Write your three question qualifying script and test it on your last twenty inbound enquiries. Measure how often three questions are enough.
  2. If you run HubSpot, connect ChatGPT Ads and run a small campaign purely to see what the attribution looks like in your own pipeline.
  3. If you are on Shopify outside the United States, note 23 September as the date the ChatGPT Ads app reaches your market, and decide before then whether you want a catalogue live in it.
  4. Decide who owns ad copy if you enable text customisation. The rewrite is automatic, the liability is not.
  5. Do not rebuild your website for this. The unit of work is a conversation, and conversations are cheaper to prototype than pages.
faqs: What is a Sponsored Agent in ChatGPT?

It is an ad unit OpenAI began testing on 16 September 2026. After a user sees a relevant ad in ChatGPT, they can choose to start a clearly labeled conversation with an agent funded by that business, ask follow up questions, and then follow a link to the business's website. OpenAI says the sponsored conversation is distinct from ChatGPT's own answers.
Can my business buy a Sponsored Agent today?

No. OpenAI says Sponsored Agents are being tested with select advertisers in the United States. The rest of the September 16 release, including the Ads Manager plugin, generated creative, and the HubSpot and Shopify integrations, is available more widely.
Does the Sponsored Agent see what the user already told ChatGPT?

OpenAI's announcement says the conversation with a Sponsored Agent is separate from the original conversation the user started in ChatGPT. So the sponsored agent does not inherit that context, even though OpenAI's opt in text customisation can adapt the ad headline to the conversation.
How does this change cost per lead reporting?

The click moves to the end of the interaction rather than the start, so click through rate is no longer comparable with a search channel. The practical model becomes cost per sponsored conversation multiplied by the rate at which those conversations produce a qualified enquiry.
What should a home services business do about Angi being in the pilot?

Assume the marketplace will own the generic query and compete on specificity instead. Write the short qualifying script that separates real jobs from enquiries, make sure your own phone and chat intake runs it reliably, and treat the marketplace lead price as the ceiling you are trying to beat.
Is the Shopify ChatGPT Ads app available outside the United States?

OpenAI says United States based Shopify merchants can use the ChatGPT Ads app in the Shopify App Store now, and that the app becomes available internationally, in markets where ChatGPT Ads are available, starting 23 September 2026.
